intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech by wandering the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians by day, then stay for the magical transformation at dusk when food stalls fill the air with smoke and spices. Explore the labyrinthine souks of the surrounding medina, bargaining for spices, leather goods, and handwoven textiles.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Journey to the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga and embark on a sunset camel trek into the Sahara. Spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a breathtaking canopy of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, sip mint tea, and wake before dawn to witness a spectacular desert sunrise over the dunes.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a local chef in a riad kitchen for a hands-on cooking class where you learn to prepare authentic Moroccan dishes such as lamb tagine with preserved lemon, harira soup, and honey-drenched pastilla. Begin with a guided tour of the spice souks to source fresh ingredients like ras el hanout, saffron, and argan oil before cooking and dining together.

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back into the grandeur of Moroccan imperial history with a self-guided or locally led tour of the 19th-century Bahia Palace, adorned with intricate zellige tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush courtyards. Continue to the nearby Saadian Tombs, a hidden necropolis of the 16th-century Saadian dynasty rediscovered in 1917, featuring stunning marble and stucco craftsmanship.

experiences.name: Ksar of Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley Drive
experiences.description: Travel through the dramatic Atlas Mountain passes to the UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) of Aït Benhaddou, a stunning example of southern Moroccan earthen clay architecture and a famous film location for Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue into the lush Draa Valley, dotted with ancient kasbahs, date palm oases, and Berber villages, stopping for a traditional lunch of mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) at a local auberge.
experiences.location: Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take the 19 bus or a shared petit taxi (negotiate firmly, ~50–70 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the medina. Check in, freshen up, and take a short stroll around the quiet night streets of Derb Sidi Bouloukat to get your bearings.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snack
meals.dinner: If hungry on arrival, grab a quick msemen (Moroccan flatbread) or harira soup from a late-night street stall near Jemaa el-Fna square (~10–15 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival simple. Exchange a small amount of cash at the airport (ATMs available). The medina streets are narrow – confirm the hotel address in Arabic before arrival. Rest well for a full day tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at a local café near the hotel – mint tea, msemen, amlou (almond-argan dip), and hard-boiled eggs (~20–30 MAD). Then walk to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (free exterior viewing) and head into the historic medina souks. Explore Souk Semmarine, Souk des Épices, and the dyers' quarter. Bargain respectfully and enjoy the sensory overload.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD) – a stunning 19th-century riad palace with intricate tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Afterward, walk to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and browse the old Jewish market. Stop at Place des Ferblantiers to see lantern craftsmen at work.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Jemaa el-Fna square at sunset – the main square transforms into a massive open-air spectacle with snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls. Eat dinner at the square's food stalls (stall numbers are posted – choose busy ones for freshness): grilled merguez, kefta brochettes, snail soup, and fresh orange juice (~40–60 MAD total).

meals.breakfast: Local café near hotel – mint tea, msemen, amlou (~25 MAD)
meals.lunch: Street food in the souks – harira soup + bread + dates (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls – grilled meats, salads, fresh juice (~50 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. The medina is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Watch for motorbikes in narrow alleys. Avoid unofficial 'guides' who approach you unsolicited.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD) – a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis hidden for centuries. Arrive early to beat crowds. Then walk to the El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD), a vast 16th-century palace complex with panoramic views from the ramparts and resident storks nesting on the walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entrance ~70 MAD) – one of the most ornate Islamic schools in North Africa, with stunning zellige tilework, carved stucco, and a serene courtyard. Afterward, visit the nearby Museum of Marrakech (entrance ~50 MAD) housed in a 19th-century palace. Spend the late afternoon wandering the northern medina souks around Souk Haddadine (blacksmiths).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a local restaurant in the medina – try a traditional tagine (chicken with preserved lemon or lamb with prunes) at a no-frills local eatery like Restaurant Haj Boujemaa or similar (~40–60 MAD for a full meal). End the evening with a walk through the lit-up Jemaa el-Fna.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby café – coffee, bread, olive oil, honey (~20 MAD)
meals.lunch: Cheap medina restaurant – couscous Friday special or tagine + bread (~35–45 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local medina restaurant – tagine + mint tea (~50–60 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sahara tour (Day 4–6) today if not already done. Budget group tours from Marrakech to Merzouga (3 days/2 nights) cost approximately 800–1,200 MAD per person including transport, accommodation, and camel ride. Ask your hotel to recommend reputable operators.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (around 07:00) on a shared group tour minibus to the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi). The journey takes approximately 9–10 hours with scenic stops. First stop: Ait Benhaddou – a UNESCO-listed ksar (fortified village) used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the ancient mud-brick citadel on foot (~10 MAD entry or free from outside).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the dramatic Draa Valley and Dadès Gorges. Stop at Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') for a quick lunch break. Pass through the Valley of Roses and the Todra Gorge area, with towering 300-meter canyon walls – a brief photo stop is usually included.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga at sunset. Mount camels for a 45-minute ride into the Sahara to your desert camp. Watch the sunset over the dunes (one of Morocco's most iconic experiences). Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner at the camp (included in tour), followed by live Gnawa music around a campfire under a sky full of stars.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure or packed snack (~15–20 MAD)
meals.lunch: Roadside café in Ouarzazate – tagine or sandwich (~35–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Included in desert camp tour – Berber tagine, bread, mint tea

day_by_day.notes: Pack a light jacket – desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Bring a headscarf/buff for sand. Charge all devices before leaving Marrakech. The camel ride and camp are typically included in group tour packages.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 06:00) to climb the Erg Chebbi dunes for a breathtaking desert sunrise – one of the most memorable moments of the trip. The silence and golden light over the sea of sand dunes is extraordinary. Return to camp for a simple Berber breakfast of bread, olive oil, honey, and mint tea (included).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Merzouga village on foot or by rented bicycle (~30–50 MAD/hour). Visit the local Gnawa musicians' quarter, the small lake (Dayet Srji) where flamingos sometimes gather in spring, and the Khamlia village known for its sub-Saharan Gnawa music tradition. Alternatively, try sandboarding on the dunes (boards sometimes available at camp).
day_by_day.evening: Second night in the desert camp or a budget auberge in Merzouga (~100–150 MAD for a dorm/basic room if not included in tour). Enjoy another evening of stargazing – with minimal light pollution, the Milky Way is clearly visible in March. Dinner at the camp or a local Merzouga restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp – Berber bread, honey, olive oil, mint tea
meals.lunch: Local Merzouga café or village restaurant – tagine or omelette (~30–40 MAD)
meals.dinner: Camp dinner (included) or local auberge restaurant – tagine (~40–50 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: March weather in the Sahara: days can reach 25–30°C, nights 5–10°C. Stay hydrated. If you want extra activities like quad biking, negotiate prices locally (~150–200 MAD/hour). Protect your camera from sand.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Merzouga (around 07:00–08:00) on the return journey to Marrakech via a different southern route. Stop at the Draa Valley oasis towns – lush palm groves stretching for kilometers along the riverbed, a striking contrast to the desert. Brief stop at Agdz or Zagora for photos and a tea break.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Anti-Atlas mountains with dramatic landscapes. Stop at Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m elevation) – the highest paved mountain pass in North Africa, with sweeping Atlas Mountain views. Arrive back in Marrakech in the late afternoon (~17:00–18:00). Check back into Hotel Aday and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed final evening in Marrakech. Visit the Mellah spice market for last-minute souvenir shopping – saffron, argan oil, ras el hanout spice mix, and leather goods are good value buys. Dinner at a rooftop restaurant near Jemaa el-Fna with views of the square – look for set menus (menu du jour) for best value (~60–80 MAD).

meals.breakfast: Included at camp or quick café stop on the road
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in Draa Valley or packed lunch from camp (~30–40 MAD if not included)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant near Jemaa el-Fna – set menu tagine + salad + tea (~70 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The return journey is equally scenic. Sit on the left side of the minibus for the best mountain views through Tizi n'Tichka. Confirm your hotel reservation is still active for tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Visit the Majorelle Garden (entrance ~70 MAD) – a stunning botanical garden with cobalt-blue buildings, exotic cacti, and the YSL Museum (optional, ~100 MAD extra). Arrive at opening time (09:00) to avoid crowds. The garden is a 20-minute walk or short taxi ride from the medina. Afterward, browse the Gueliz neighborhood (new city) for a different, more European side of Marrakech.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the medina for final souvenir shopping in the souks. Visit a traditional hammam for a budget scrub and steam session – try a local neighborhood hammam (not tourist-oriented) for ~30–50 MAD including kessa glove scrub. This is an authentic Moroccan cultural experience. Pack your bags and enjoy a final mint tea at a rooftop café overlooking the medina rooftops.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a local medina restaurant – splurge slightly on your last night with a pastilla (sweet-savory pigeon or chicken pie) or a mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) if available (~60–80 MAD). Head to the airport with plenty of time (allow 1.5 hours before departure). Take the 19 bus or negotiate a taxi (~60–80 MAD to airport).

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at a medina café – msemen, amlou, mint tea (~25–30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Gueliz or medina – sandwich marocain or bissara (fava bean soup) (~20–30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local medina restaurant – pastilla or tagine + dessert (~70–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate: Accommodations ~150–200 MAD/night, Sahara tour ~900–1,100 MAD, daily food ~100–150 MAD, entrance fees ~300 MAD total, transport ~200 MAD. Total 7-day budget estimate: approximately 2,500–3,500 MAD (≈$250–350 USD) excluding flights. Tip generously where service was good – 10–15 MAD is appreciated.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-arranged airport transfer or petit taxi (~80–100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store or ask the hotel for a late-night recommendation close to Derb Sidi Bouloukat

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – jet lag and a late arrival mean rest is the priority. Confirm your hotel has 24-hour reception or arrange a late check-in in advance. Exchange some currency to MAD at the airport for taxis and tips.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Then walk 10 minutes to the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square to soak in the morning atmosphere – orange juice vendors, bread sellers, and locals heading to work. Visit the nearby Koutoubia Mosque (exterior) and stroll through the surrounding gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a stunning 19th-century riad-style palace with intricate tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Afterward, wander through the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and browse the spice souks and artisan stalls in the surrounding medina lanes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a vibrant open-air spectacle – snake charmers, storytellers, and food stalls. Dine at one of the evening food stalls (stall numbers 1–10 are popular) for a lively, authentic experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café des Épices nearby – mint tea, msemen (flatbread), honey, and amlou (almond-argan dip) for ~30–50 MAD
meals.lunch: Restaurant Nomad in the Medina – modern Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views, budget ~100–150 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls – harira soup, merguez sandwiches, and grilled kefta for ~60–100 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – medina streets are cobblestone and uneven. Keep a small bag close to you in crowded areas. Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at 40–50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis hidden for centuries. Then head to the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) – a vast 16th-century palace complex with storks nesting on the ramparts and panoramic views from the terraces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon getting lost in the famous souks of Marrakech – Souk Semmarine (textiles), Souk Cherratin (leather), and Souk Haddadine (metalwork). Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), one of the most ornate Islamic schools in North Africa, featuring stunning zellige tilework and carved stucco.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Moroccan hammam experience at a mid-range local hammam such as Hammam Dar el-Bacha (~150–200 MAD for the full experience including scrub). Afterward, dine at a riad restaurant for a proper sit-down Moroccan feast.

meals.breakfast: Café Clock Marrakech – avocado toast meets Moroccan pastries, ~50–80 MAD
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Medina restaurant near Ben Youssef – tagine of the day with bread and salad for ~80–120 MAD
meals.dinner: Riad Yima restaurant or Le Foundouk – lamb pastilla or chicken tagine with preserved lemon, ~150–200 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in advance if possible, especially for evenings. The Ben Youssef Madrasa can get crowded mid-morning – aim to arrive right when it opens. Carry a light layer as some historic sites can be cool inside.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (around 7:00–8:00 AM) from Marrakech by shared or private transfer toward the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley route (Ouarzazate direction). The drive takes approximately 8–9 hours to reach Merzouga/Erg Chebbi. Stop at the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) for photos of the dramatic Atlas Mountain scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley, stopping at the fortified ksar (village) of Aït Benhaddou – a UNESCO World Heritage Site and famous film location (Game of Thrones, Gladiator). Explore the ancient earthen citadel (~30 MAD entry) and cross the river on stepping stones. Continue driving toward the desert, passing through Ouarzazate and the Valley of Roses.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Merzouga (Erg Chebbi) around sunset. Mount a camel for a 45-minute ride into the golden dunes to your desert camp. Watch the sunset over the Sahara from the top of a dune. Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner at the camp under a sky full of stars.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure – bread, jam, coffee, ~30–50 MAD or included with stay
meals.lunch: Roadside Berber restaurant near Aït Benhaddou – tagine and Moroccan salad, ~80–100 MAD
meals.dinner: Included at the desert camp – traditional Berber meal: harira, tagine, couscous, Moroccan mint tea, and fresh fruit (~included in camp price or ~200 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book your desert camp in advance – mid-range options like Sahara Desert Camp Merzouga or similar offer private tents with basic amenities for ~400–700 MAD per person including dinner and breakfast. Bring a warm layer – desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Shared transport (grand taxi or shared minibus) costs ~200–300 MAD per person; private transfer ~800–1,200 MAD.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the dunes and watch the sunrise over the Sahara – one of the most breathtaking experiences in Morocco. After breakfast at camp, explore the Merzouga village on foot or by quad bike (~200–300 MAD/hour). Visit a local Gnawa musician family for a cultural music session if arranged through your camp.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey toward Marrakech, taking the northern route through the Ziz Valley and Todra Gorge. Stop at the dramatic Todra Gorge – towering 300-meter limestone canyon walls with a river running through. Walk through the gorge (~1 hour) and interact with local Berber villagers.
day_by_day.evening: Continue driving and stop overnight in the town of Ouarzazate or Boumalne Dades to break the journey. Check into a mid-range guesthouse/riad. Explore the town in the evening and enjoy a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp – Berber bread, olive oil, honey, eggs, mint tea
meals.lunch: Local restaurant at Todra Gorge – fresh trout from the river (a regional specialty), salad, and bread for ~100–130 MAD
meals.dinner: Riad or local restaurant in Ouarzazate/Boumalne – lamb mechoui or vegetable couscous, ~120–160 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: The Todra Gorge is most dramatic in the morning light but still beautiful in the afternoon. Wear sturdy shoes for the gorge walk. If time allows, a short detour to the Dades Gorge (Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs) is highly recommended – the winding road is spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Return drive to Marrakech (approximately 4–5 hours from Ouarzazate). Stop at the Kasbah Taourirt in Ouarzazate before departing – a well-preserved 20th-century kasbah and former Glaoui clan stronghold (entry ~20 MAD). Also pass by the Atlas Film Studios (exterior view), the largest film studio in the world by area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by early afternoon. Check back into Hotel Aday. Visit the Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD) – a stunning botanical garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later owned by Yves Saint Laurent, featuring vivid cobalt-blue structures and exotic plants. The adjacent Berber Museum (included in ticket) is excellent for cultural context.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your last evening in the Medina doing any remaining souvenir shopping in the souks. Visit the rooftop terrace of a café overlooking Jemaa el-Fna for sunset views. Enjoy a farewell Moroccan dinner at a mid-range restaurant.

meals.breakfast: At the guesthouse in Ouarzazate before departure – included or ~50 MAD
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near Majorelle Garden – Café Bousafsaf or similar, Moroccan sandwich (kefta or merguez) and fresh juice, ~60–80 MAD
meals.dinner: Dar Zitoun or Terrasse des Épices in the Medina – slow-cooked lamb shank tagine or bastilla au pigeon, ~180–250 MAD per person for a special farewell meal

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden gets very busy in the afternoon – try to arrive right when it opens or later in the day. Book the farewell dinner in advance as popular Medina restaurants fill up quickly. Use this evening to pack and prepare for departure.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely final morning in Marrakech. Take a slow walk through the quieter morning medina streets before the crowds arrive. Visit the Mouassine Fountain and the Mouassine Mosque area – one of the most photogenic and authentic corners of the old city. Browse the Mellah market for last-minute local spices, argan oil, or preserved lemons to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final mint tea and pastilla (sweet pigeon pie) at a traditional café. If time allows, visit the Musée de Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) housed in a beautiful 19th-century palace near Ben Youssef for a final dose of Moroccan art and history.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for the taxi ride and airport procedures.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday or Café des Épices – msemen, beghrir (honeycomb pancakes), argan oil, mint tea, ~40–60 MAD
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a medina café or riad – Moroccan salad plate and harira soup, ~70–100 MAD
meals.dinner: Airport meal or early dinner before heading to the airport – keep it simple and budget ~100–150 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Marrakech taxis to the airport cost ~80–120 MAD (negotiate before getting in or use a metered petit taxi). Allow extra time during busy periods. Declare any argan oil or food products at customs if flying internationally. Keep a small amount of MAD for tips and last-minute purchases – leftover dirhams cannot easily be exchanged outside Morocco.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Hotel Aday in the heart of the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome mint tea and light refreshments prepared by the riad staff. Settle into your suite and rest after the journey.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at departure airport
meals.lunch: On the flight or at departure airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night mezze and Moroccan pastries arranged by Hotel Aday upon arrival — dates, msemen flatbread, honey, and argan oil dips served in your suite

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer with a luxury chauffeur service (e.g., Marrakech Luxury Transfers). Confirm with Hotel Aday for a late check-in and request a welcome tray. Keep Day 1 light — the Medina's narrow derbs can be disorienting at night for first-timers.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the riad rooftop terrace. Then embark on a guided private walking tour of the Medina starting from Derb Sidi Bouloukat. Explore the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square in the calm morning hours before the crowds arrive. Visit the 14th-century Ben Youssef Madrasa, one of the most ornate Islamic colleges in North Africa — admire its intricate zellige tilework, carved stucco, and cedar woodwork with a private expert guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace, a stunning 19th-century royal complex with lush gardens and painted ceilings, followed by a stroll through the Mellah (historic Jewish quarter) and the covered souks. Engage in a curated private shopping experience in the artisan souks — leather goods, handwoven carpets, and silver jewelry — with your guide helping navigate and negotiate authentically.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the rooftop of a nearby luxury riad bar overlooking the Koutoubia Mosque minaret. Dinner at Le Foundouk, a celebrated fine-dining restaurant in a restored 18th-century caravanserai near the souks, offering refined Moroccan cuisine — try the pigeon pastilla, slow-cooked lamb tagine with preserved lemon, and orange blossom crème brûlée.

meals.breakfast: Riad rooftop breakfast — fresh-squeezed orange juice, Moroccan pancakes (baghrir and msemen), honey, amlou (argan-almond spread), soft-boiled eggs, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Café des Épices on Place Rahba Kedima — rooftop terrace with views over the spice market; try the harira soup, kefta brochettes, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.dinner: Le Foundouk, Rue du Souk des Fassis — refined Moroccan tasting menu with wine pairing; budget approximately 800–1,200 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Ben Youssef Madrasa tickets in advance online to avoid queues. Hire a licensed private guide through your hotel concierge for the full-day Medina tour — approximately 600–900 MAD for a half-day. Dress modestly for religious and historic sites (covered shoulders and knees).

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Saadian Tombs, a hidden royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring exquisite Andalusian-Moroccan architecture. Continue to the El Badi Palace ruins — a vast 16th-century palace complex once described as one of the wonders of the world. Explore the sunken gardens, stork nests, and the underground passages with your private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a traditional hammam and spa experience at a premium hammam such as Hammam de la Rose or Les Bains de Marrakech — enjoy a black soap scrub (kessa), ghassoul clay mask, and a full-body argan oil massage. Return refreshed and spend the late afternoon exploring the Mellah's antique dealers and the Maison de la Photographie for a cultural interlude.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Dar Yacout, one of Marrakech's most legendary palatial dining experiences — a restored 17th-century mansion with candlelit courtyards, live Gnawa music, and a lavish multi-course Moroccan feast. Expect couscous royale, bastilla au lait for dessert, and an unforgettable atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Aday riad breakfast — seasonal fruit platter, Moroccan crepes, olive tapenade, fresh cheese, and spiced coffee
meals.lunch: Light post-hammam lunch at Nomad Restaurant, Derb Aarjan — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with a rooftop terrace; try the lamb merguez flatbread and beetroot hummus
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout, 79 Sidi Ahmed Soussi — iconic palatial dinner experience; reservation essential, approximately 700–1,000 MAD per person including welcome cocktail

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam session at least 2 days in advance through your hotel concierge. Saadian Tombs can get crowded by mid-morning — aim to arrive at opening (9:00 AM). Dar Yacout requires advance reservation; request a courtyard table for the best ambiance.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (7:00 AM) by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the Sahara Desert — the journey takes approximately 8–9 hours via the spectacular Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m altitude) through the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at the Kasbah Aït Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and ancient fortified village that has served as a backdrop for films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Guided walk through the ksar with a local expert.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley — a lush palm-lined oasis stretching for miles — stopping at a local Berber family home for a traditional mint tea ceremony and a glimpse into nomadic life. Arrive in the Merzouga/Erg Chebbi dune region by late afternoon. Check in to your luxury desert camp or boutique desert lodge (e.g., Scarabeo Camp or Dar Ahlam).
day_by_day.evening: Mount camels at sunset for a guided camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes — the largest sand dunes in Morocco, reaching up to 150 meters. Reach the peak of a dune for a breathtaking Sahara sunset. Dinner under the stars at your private luxury camp — traditional Berber music around a campfire, a multi-course dinner served on Moroccan rugs, and a sky full of stars with zero light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast box prepared by Hotel Aday — croissants, fruit, cheese, and thermos of coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop in Ouarzazate at Restaurant Chez Dimitri or a curated local restaurant — harira, tagine, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Private luxury desert camp dinner — Berber-spiced lamb mechoui, vegetable couscous, Moroccan salads, and pastilla; served under the stars with traditional Gnawa musicians

day_by_day.notes: The drive is long but extraordinarily scenic — the Tizi n'Tichka pass can be cold in March, so bring a layer. Pre-book your luxury desert camp well in advance (Scarabeo Camp, Dar Ahlam, or Erg Chebbi Luxury Camp are top-tier options). Bring a warm jacket for the desert night — temperatures in March can drop to 5–8°C after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (5:30 AM) for a private sunrise camel or quad bike ride to the top of the Erg Chebbi dunes — witness one of the most spectacular sunrises on earth as the dunes shift from deep purple to gold. Return to camp for a lavish Berber breakfast. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a 4x4 desert excursion to visit a nomadic Tuareg family encampment and a fossil market in Erfoud.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart the desert and begin the scenic return journey westward. Stop at the Todra Gorge — a dramatic canyon with 300-meter-high rose-colored limestone walls carved by the Todra River. Walk through the gorge floor with a guide and enjoy the surreal landscape. Continue to your overnight stop in the Dades Valley.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a luxury kasbah hotel in the Dades Valley (e.g., Kasbah Tamadot or a boutique kasbah lodge). Enjoy a private terrace dinner overlooking the Valley of Roses with a traditional Moroccan feast and local Dades Valley wine.

meals.breakfast: Luxury desert camp Berber breakfast — msemen with honey and argan oil, fresh fruit, Berber omelette, and spiced coffee served on the dunes
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the camp or a local café near Todra Gorge — sandwiches, olives, cheese, and fresh orange juice
meals.dinner: Kasbah hotel terrace dinner — slow-roasted lamb with prunes and almonds, Dades rose petal salad, and traditional Moroccan pastries with mint tea

day_by_day.notes: Set an alarm for 5:15 AM for the sunrise experience — it is the highlight of the desert stay and not to be missed. The Todra Gorge is most dramatic in the morning light but remains impressive all day. The Valley of Roses is particularly beautiful in late March when roses begin to bloom.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in the Dades Valley — optional hike through the Dades Gorge with a local Berber guide, exploring the dramatic rock formations known as 'monkey fingers.' Visit a local cooperative producing rose water and argan oil products — a fascinating insight into Berber women's cooperatives and sustainable production. Purchase premium rose water and argan oil directly from the source.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Marrakech via the scenic Route of the Kasbahs — stopping at the fortified village of Skoura and its ancient palm grove. Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon. Check back in to Hotel Aday. Freshen up and enjoy a private rooftop sunset moment over the Medina skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Marrakech — begin with cocktails at the Sky Bar of La Mamounia Hotel (one of the world's great luxury hotels, open to non-guests for drinks). Dinner at Hakkasan Marrakech at La Mamounia — a world-renowned Cantonese fine-dining restaurant with a Moroccan twist, offering an extraordinary fusion tasting menu in an opulent setting.

meals.breakfast: Kasbah hotel breakfast — fresh-baked bread, local honey, goat cheese, seasonal fruit, and Berber tea
meals.lunch: En route stop in Ouarzazate or Ait Benhaddou — traditional tagine at a local restaurant with panoramic kasbah views
meals.dinner: Hakkasan at La Mamounia, Avenue Bab Jdid — premium Cantonese-Moroccan fusion tasting menu with cocktail pairing; approximately 1,200–1,800 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: The return drive from Dades to Marrakech is approximately 5–6 hours — depart by 9:00 AM to arrive comfortably before sunset. La Mamounia's Sky Bar and Hakkasan require advance reservations — book through your hotel concierge. This is an ideal evening for a special occasion dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning in the Medina. Enjoy a slow breakfast at the riad. Take a peaceful early morning walk through the Djemaa el-Fna square — magical and nearly empty at dawn. Visit the Jardin Majorelle, the iconic cobalt-blue garden and villa designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent — a serene and visually stunning farewell to Marrakech. Visit the adjacent Musée Yves Saint Laurent for a world-class fashion and art experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for checkout. Last-minute souvenir shopping in the Gueliz neighborhood (the modern French quarter) — visit concept stores like 33 Rue Majorelle for curated Moroccan luxury goods, leather bags, and artisan jewelry. Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech — carry the memories of the Sahara dunes, ancient kasbahs, and the intoxicating scents of the Medina souks.

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast — a celebratory spread of all Moroccan favorites: msemen, baghrir, honey, amlou, fresh orange juice, and a pot of premium Moroccan mint tea
meals.lunch: Brunch at Café du Livre in Gueliz or Atay Café — avocado toast with chermoula, Moroccan eggs, and fresh-pressed juices in a relaxed modern setting
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining — or an early dinner at the airport's premium lounge if time permits

day_by_day.notes: Jardin Majorelle opens at 8:00 AM — arrive early to enjoy it before the crowds. Book Musée Yves Saint Laurent tickets online in advance. Allow at least 2 hours at the airport before departure — Marrakech Menara Airport can be busy. Ensure all purchased goods (argan oil, spices, leather) are properly packed to comply with airline regulations.
